newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends firmer on dollar supplies.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends firmer on dollar supplies.

text.p: The won closed firmer against the dollar on Tuesday due to continued dollar supplies from exporters and foreign stock investors, dealers said.
But fears of the central bank's dollar buying intervention limited the won's rise, they said.
"Dollar inflows continued today. But dollar sales were limited because of the belief the central bank does not want the dollar below 888.00 level," said a domestic bank dealer.
The won closed at 888.30 against Monday's closing of 888.90. It opened at 888.60 and moved between 888.10 and 888.80.
The won's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 888.40 on Wednesday compared with 888.50 today.
"On Wednesday, traders are likely to unwind their dollar positions to test whether the central bank moves back its defence line," said a foreign bank dealer.
Most dealers forecast trading would be dull on Wednesday in the absence of fresh factors.
